stemMd: What is the main point of "The translator's margin"?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Readers should be required to study every note before reading a text.

options.label: B
options.textMd: A translation can pursue readable prose while making important interpretive choices visible.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Earlier translations should never be consulted.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A dictionary always supplies one exact English equivalent.

explanationMd: The example develops a compromise between fluent reading and transparent interpretation. The conclusion expressly keeps fluency as a goal while allowing scrutiny of consequential choices.

distractorRationale.c: The earlier version provides a comparison; no such prohibition is argued.
distractorRationale.d: The passage explains why no single everyday word captures all associations.
distractorRationale.a: The back-note arrangement lets readers choose.
